sections.html:
Skagit County covers about 1,730 square miles of the Puget Sound region and holds 132,975 people. Its seat and biggest city is Mount Vernon. Property types vary widely: the Skagit River valley is tulip, blueberry and strawberry country, Fidalgo and Guemes islands have shoreline lots, and the east side climbs into the Cascade foothills.

Owner-occupied homes have a median value of $545,100, and owners live in 70.1% of housing units. With 25.0% of residents at least 65 years old, the senior exemption described below matters to a lot of local owners.

The Assessor decides values, sets levies and approves exemptions. The Treasurer mails bills and takes payments. A separate Board of Equalization hears disputes over value.

OfficeResponsibilityContact
TreasurerCollects tax, accepts payments, handles late-payment questions700 S. 2nd Street, Room 205, Mount Vernon, WA 98273; 360-416-1750; mail to PO Box 518
AssessorValues property, sets levies, approves exemptions360-416-1780; assessor@skagitcountywa.gov
Board of EqualizationHears assessed value appeals700 S. 2nd Street, Room 100, Mount Vernon; clerk at 360-416-1126

If Mount Vernon is a long drive, the Concrete satellite office at 45770 A Main Street takes cash, check or money order.

sections.h2: Due dates and how to pay
sections.html:
Each year's tax is split into an April 30 half and an October 31 half. Small bills under $50 are payable in one piece by April 30 (RCW 84.56.020). Your next date is April 30, 2027.

Options for paying:

  • Walk in to the Treasurer in Mount Vernon and pay with cash, check, money order or card.
  • Use a drop box at 700 S. 2nd Street, either at the west end of the horseshoe parking lot or upstairs outside Room 205. Boxes take checks and money orders only.
  • Call 1-866-791-3392. The processor charges $3.95 plus 2.35% on debit and credit cards, or $1.00 on checks.
  • Enroll in auto-pay, which draws from a U.S. checking or savings account on April 30 and October 31, or takes the whole year on April 30. Forms are due April 15 for spring and October 15 for fall.

Be careful with envelopes. Same-day postmarks are no longer guaranteed, and only a postmark on or before the due date counts as on time. Mail well ahead or use a drop box.

After the due date, interest runs on the whole year's tax beginning May 1. The Treasurer, at 360-416-1750, can give you the exact payoff to send.

For taxes levied from 2023 forward, a home with four or fewer units, including a manufactured home, pays 9% a year and no penalty. Other real property and personal property pay 12% a year, with a 3% penalty if still delinquent June 1 and 8% more on December 1 (RCW 84.56.020).

Relief is narrow. The treasurer must waive interest and penalties if the county never sent the notice. Missing a payment on a personal residence after a spouse's death, or a parent's or stepparent's death, can also be forgiven if you tell the treasurer within 60 days of the due date (RCW 84.56.025). Payment plans and partial payments are possible, with money applied to the oldest year first.

Your Notice of Value shows the filing deadline for the Skagit County Board of Equalization. Under RCW 84.40.038 a petition is timely by July 1 or 30 days after the notice was mailed, whichever comes later. The notice reflects market value on January 1 and sets the tax due the next year. Owners whose value stayed the same and who got no notice are still held to the deadline.

A late petition may be accepted if it arrives within a reasonable time and shows good cause, for example a serious illness or a postal delay the Postal Service documented. Ask the clerk at 360-416-1126.

Hearing basics:

  • Ten minutes for you, ten for the Assessor, then your reply.
  • The Assessor's number starts out presumed correct. To change it you need clear, cogent and convincing evidence of an error (RCW 84.40.0301).
  • Useful proof includes comparable sales close to the valuation date, contractor repair estimates and independent appraisals. Listings do not count.
  • Additional documents are due 21 business days ahead.
  • Expect the process to take 6 to 12 months.

The board cannot weigh the size of your bill, hardship or how large the increase was. If you lose, you have 30 days to go to the Washington State Board of Tax Appeals. The Assessor's next reinspection cycle begins in the Mount Vernon School District and uses street-level and aerial imagery.

Skagit's main relief program serves owners 61 or older, owners with disabilities and owners with a 40% VA disability rating. The income ceiling rises to $78,000 in 2027.

To qualify, add up disposable income for everyone who owns and lives in the home: adjusted gross income plus untaxed items such as Social Security, pensions and annuities. Then subtract either $7,500 per person (you and a spouse or domestic partner) or your real qualifying costs, such as prescriptions, Medicare premiums and care. Beginning in 2027 you may also subtract up to $6,000 of rent collected from living space in your home. The Assessor, at 360-416-1780, will walk through the worksheet with you.

Every statement carries a notice about the exemption and the state deferral program (RCW 84.56.020). If fire or another event destroys part or all of a property, a value reduction can be claimed within three years of the damage (RCW 84.70.010).

Some charges are special assessments that fall outside the 1% cap on regular levies. The Assessor does not set them. Each district or program writes its own budget and divides it by acreage, value or some other formula.

  • Diking and drainage districts look after dikes, ditches and pump stations in their areas.
  • The Clean Water Assessment supports the county's Clean Water Program, aimed at bacterial pollution, including Samish Bay shellfish beds, along with septic repairs and water monitoring.
  • The County Drainage Utility pays for pump stations, piping, tide gates, ditches and similar stormwater work.

Two homes assessed at the same value can still owe different totals, because each belongs to its own mix of city, school, fire and library districts.

Whatever is owed on the parcel must come out of your proceeds, or the buyer takes on the problem. Request a payoff from the Treasurer covering each unpaid year before you say yes to an offer.

A sale also triggers Washington's real estate excise tax. It is payable to the county treasurer on the sale date, even if the deed is recorded later, and the seller usually pays. For sales from January 1, 2027 the Department of Revenue schedule is 1.1% up to $551,000, 1.28% from $551,000 to $1,551,000, 2.75% up to $3,051,000 and 3.0% beyond that. Add the local rate; the Treasurer can give you the combined amount.

Delay is risky. At three years past delinquency the treasurer must issue certificates of delinquency and start foreclosure (RCW 84.64.050). An income-qualified owner who lives in the home may get interest and penalties waived shortly before that mark if foreclosure is already moving (RCW 84.56.020).

A cash buyer can close without waiting on a lender, and the title company pays the Treasurer out of your proceeds. Whichever route you take, get the payoff in writing first.

faqs.q: When are Skagit County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Half is due April 30 and half October 31, or the whole bill April 30 if it is under $50. Your next date is April 30, 2027. Interest begins May 1 and is figured on the full year.

faqs.q: Can I still appeal my Skagit County value?
faqs.a: The deadline is printed on your Notice of Value. If it is past, the Board of Equalization may accept a late petition for good cause, such as serious illness or documented postal delay. Ask the clerk at 360-416-1126 and have your parcel number ready.

faqs.q: What interest rate applies to late Skagit County tax?
faqs.a: A home with four or fewer units pays 9% a year and no penalty. Other property pays 12% a year, a 3% penalty after June 1 and 8% more after December 1. Phone the Treasurer at 360-416-1750 for your parcel's payoff.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a Skagit County property tax question?
faqs.a: Use the Treasurer, 360-416-1750, for bills, payments and payoffs. Use the Assessor, 360-416-1780, for values and exemptions. The Board of Equalization clerk, 360-416-1126, handles appeals.

faqs.q: How long can Skagit County property tax stay unpaid before foreclosure?
faqs.a: Three years past delinquency, the treasurer must begin foreclosure. No certificate can be filed when the delinquent tax is $100 or less (RCW 84.64.050). Pay or sell well before then, since interest grows each month.
